front: Excusez-moi, où est la station de métro la plus proche ?
pronunciation: [ex-kü-zay-MWAH, oo eh lah stah-SYOHN duh may-TROH lah plü PROSH]
back: Excuse me, where's the nearest metro station?
context: Always start with 'Excusez-moi' or 'Bonjour' before asking a stranger anything.

front: Allez tout droit, puis tournez à gauche.
pronunciation: [ah-lay too DRWAH, pwee toor-nay ah GOHSH]
back: Go straight ahead, then turn left.
context: Careful: 'tout droit' = straight ahead, but 'à droite' = to the right.

front: C'est la deuxième rue à droite.
pronunciation: [seh lah duh-zyem rü ah DRWAHT]
back: It's the second street on the right.
context: Ordinals: premier/première, deuxième, troisième…

front: C'est loin d'ici ?
pronunciation: [seh lwan dee-SEE]
back: Is it far from here?
context: Answer: 'C'est à cinq minutes à pied' = it's a five-minute walk.

front: C'est à dix minutes à pied.
pronunciation: [seh tah dee mee-nüt ah PYAY]
back: It's a ten-minute walk.
context: 'À pied' (on foot) but 'en voiture', 'en bus', 'en train', 'à vélo'.

front: Je me suis perdu, vous pouvez m'aider ?
pronunciation: [zhuh muh swee pehr-DÜ, voo poo-vay meh-DAY]
back: I'm lost, can you help me?
context: 'Se perdre' = to get lost. A woman says 'perdue'.

front: Vous pouvez me montrer sur le plan ?
pronunciation: [voo poo-vay muh mohn-tray sür luh PLAHN]
back: Can you show me on the map?
context: 'Le plan' = city or metro map; 'la carte' = a larger map (country, region).

front: Un billet pour Lyon, s'il vous plaît.
pronunciation: [an bee-YEH poor lee-OHN, seel voo PLEH]
back: A ticket to Lyon, please.
context: 'Un billet' = ticket. Most train tickets are bought online or in the SNCF app.

front: Un aller simple ou un aller-retour ?
pronunciation: [an nah-lay SAN-pluh oo an nah-lay-ruh-TOOR]
back: One way or return?
context: 'Aller simple' = one way; 'aller-retour' = round trip.

front: Le train part de quel quai ?
pronunciation: [luh tran par duh kel KAY]
back: Which platform does the train leave from?
context: 'Le quai' = platform. The platform is often announced only 20 minutes before departure.

front: Le train a vingt minutes de retard.
pronunciation: [luh tran ah van mee-nüt duh ruh-TAR]
back: The train is twenty minutes late.
context: 'Avoir du retard' = to be delayed. 'Le train est supprimé' = the train is cancelled.

front: Est-ce qu'il faut changer ?
pronunciation: [es-keel foh shahn-ZHAY]
back: Do I need to change?
context: 'Changer' (de train, de ligne) = to transfer. 'Une correspondance' = a connection.

front: Prenez la ligne quatre, direction Porte de Clignancourt.
pronunciation: [pruh-nay lah leen KAT, dee-rek-SYOHN port duh klee-nyahn-KOOR]
back: Take line 4, towards Porte de Clignancourt.
context: In the Paris metro you follow lines by number and by their final stop ('direction').

front: Descendez au prochain arrêt.
pronunciation: [day-sahn-day oh proh-shan nah-REH]
back: Get off at the next stop.
context: 'Descendre' = to get off; 'monter' = to get on. 'L'arrêt' = (bus) stop.

front: Ce bus va à la gare ?
pronunciation: [suh büs vah ah lah GAR]
back: Does this bus go to the train station?
context: 'La gare' = train station; 'la gare routière' = bus station.

front: Il faut composter le billet ?
pronunciation: [eel foh kohm-pos-TAY luh bee-YEH]
back: Do I need to validate the ticket?
context: On many buses and regional trains you must validate your ticket, or risk a fine.

front: Je voudrais louer une voiture pour une semaine.
pronunciation: [zhuh voo-dreh loo-ay ün vwah-TÜR poor ün suh-MEN]
back: I'd like to rent a car for a week.
context: 'Louer' = to rent. Manual cars are still common: ask for 'une boîte automatique' if needed.

front: Le plein, s'il vous plaît.
pronunciation: [luh PLAN, seel voo PLEH]
back: Fill it up, please.
context: 'Faire le plein' = to fill the tank. 'Gazole' or 'diesel', 'sans plomb' = unleaded.

front: Il y a des bouchons sur le périphérique.
pronunciation: [eel yah day boo-SHOHN sür luh pay-ree-fay-REEK]
back: There are traffic jams on the ring road.
context: 'Un bouchon' (cork) = traffic jam. Le périphérique is the ring road around Paris.

front: Où est-ce que je peux garer la voiture ?
pronunciation: [oo es-kuh zhuh puh gah-ray lah vwah-TÜR]
back: Where can I park the car?
context: 'Se garer' = to park. 'Le parking' = car park.

front: Je prends le vélo pour aller au travail.
pronunciation: [zhuh prahn luh vay-LOH poor ah-lay oh trah-VAHY]
back: I bike to work.
context: 'Prendre' + transport: prendre le bus, prendre le métro, prendre le train.

front: Le vol pour Montréal est à quelle heure ?
pronunciation: [luh vol poor mohn-ray-AHL eh tah kel UHR]
back: What time is the flight to Montreal?
context: 'Le vol' = flight (also theft!).

front: Où est l'enregistrement ?
pronunciation: [oo eh lahn-ruh-zhees-truh-MAHN]
back: Where is check-in?
context: 'Enregistrer ses bagages' = to check in your luggage.

front: J'ai seulement un bagage à main.
pronunciation: [zhay suhl-mahn an bah-gahzh ah MAN]
back: I only have hand luggage.
context: 'Un bagage à main' / 'un bagage cabine' = carry-on.

front: Mon vol a été annulé.
pronunciation: [mohn vol ah ay-TAY ah-nü-LAY]
back: My flight was cancelled.
context: Passé composé passive: 'a été' + participle.

front: Un taxi pour l'aéroport, c'est combien ?
pronunciation: [an tak-SEE poor lah-ay-roh-POR, seh kohm-BYAN]
back: How much is a taxi to the airport?
context: Paris airport taxis have fixed fares into the city.

front: Vous pouvez m'appeler un taxi ?
pronunciation: [voo poo-vay mah-puh-lay an tak-SEE]
back: Can you call me a taxi?
context: 'Appeler un taxi' = to call a taxi. 'Un VTC' = a ride-hailing car.

front: En voiture, ça prend combien de temps ?
pronunciation: [ahn vwah-TÜR, sah prahn kohm-byan duh TAHN]
back: How long does it take by car?
context: 'Ça prend' + time = it takes.

front: Il faut environ deux heures en TGV.
pronunciation: [eel foh ahn-vee-ROHN duh zuhr ahn teh-zheh-VEH]
back: It takes about two hours by TGV.
context: The TGV is France's high-speed train.

front: Attention à la marche en descendant du train.
pronunciation: [ah-tahn-SYOHN ah lah MARSH ahn day-sahn-dahn dü TRAN]
back: Mind the step when getting off the train.
context: A familiar station announcement. 'En descendant' = while getting off (gerund).

front: Le guichet est fermé, utilisez la borne automatique.
pronunciation: [luh ghee-SHEH eh fehr-MAY, ü-tee-lee-zay lah born oh-toh-mah-TEEK]
back: The ticket office is closed; use the ticket machine.
context: 'Le guichet' = counter/window; 'la borne' = kiosk/machine.

front: C'est en face de la mairie.
pronunciation: [seh tahn fas duh lah meh-REE]
back: It's opposite the town hall.
context: 'En face de' = opposite; 'à côté de' = next to; 'au coin de' = on the corner of.

front: Traversez le pont et continuez jusqu'au feu.
pronunciation: [trah-vehr-say luh POHN ay kohn-tee-nü-ay zhüs-koh FUH]
back: Cross the bridge and keep going until the traffic light.
context: 'Le feu (rouge)' = traffic light. 'Jusqu'à' = until, as far as.

front: Le prochain train pour Bordeaux part à quatorze heures dix.
pronunciation: [luh proh-shan tran poor bor-DOH par ah kah-tor-zuhr DEES]
back: The next train to Bordeaux leaves at 2:10 p.m.
context: Train times use the 24-hour clock.

front: Bon voyage !
pronunciation: [bohn vwah-YAZH]
back: Have a good trip!
context: Also: 'Bonne route !' (to someone driving).
